turns.user: Find two web sources explaining solar panel recycling and summarize them with links.
turns.assistant_text:
Here are two web sources explaining solar panel recycling:

1. **Sungrow supports clean energy goals of a Northern Rivers solar panel recycling business**  
   This article discusses the launch of Australia's first mandatory solar panel recycling scheme by the NSW government, aimed at ensuring that solar panel materials are recovered and reused rather than dumped. It highlights ReSolve Global's efforts in collecting and sorting used solar panels to keep them out of landfills and recover valuable materials.  
   [Read more here](https://www.pv-magazine-australia.com/2026/11/06/sungrow-supports-clean-energy-goals-of-a-new-northern-rivers-solar-panel-recycling-business).

2. **True Recycling: The Key to Solar Circularity**  
   This piece emphasizes the importance of true recycling in the solar industry, which involves recovering nearly all materials from solar panels to re-enter manufacturing supply chains. It discusses the challenges of incomplete recycling practices and the need for stringent recycling standards to ensure effective recovery of materials.  
   [Read more here](https://www.powermag.com/true-recycling-the-key-to-solar-circularity).

items.title: Sungrow supports clean energy goals of a Northern Rivers solar panel recycling business - pv magazine Australia
items.summary:
The NSW government has launched consultation on a proposal to introduce Australia’s first mandatory solar panel recycling scheme, aiming to ensure solar panel materials are recovered, reused and recycled rather than being dumped. Submissions close 16 November 2026. [...] Located 13 kilometres north of Byron Bay, and approximately 155 kilometres south of Brisbane, Queensland, ReSolve Global is housed in a 2,000-square-metre holding and sorting facility where used solar panels are collected, recorded, assessed and sorted, keeping used solar panels and other renewable-energy equipment out of landfill while recovering valuable materials for reuse and recycling. [...] By the start of October 2026 when ReSolve Global began operations, it had already collected more than 1,000 solar panels and is working with local industry to develop pathways for panels to be reused where appropriate or responsibly recycled and their materials recovered.

It’s longer-term vision is to expand its resource-recovery model beyond solar panels to other renewable-energy infrastructure, including batteries, inverters and wind turbine components.

items.title: Closing the Loop: Sungrow Sponsors Solar and Storage System to Power Northern Rivers Solar Recycling Hub
items.summary: ReSolve Global has established a 2,000-square-metre holding and sorting facility where used solar panels are collected, recorded, assessed and sorted.  It keeps used solar panels and other renewable-energy equipment out of landfill and recovers valuable materials for reuse and recycling. [...] As Australia's rooftop solar uptake continues to grow, so does the number of panels reaching the end of their working lives. The NSW Government recently announced consultation on Australia's first mandatory solar panel product stewardship scheme, aimed at ensuring end-of-life panels are recovered, reused and recycled. Local infrastructure that can handle this equipment will be essential as the scheme develops.

items.title: True Recycling: The Key to Solar Circularity
items.summary:
True recycling recovers all, or nearly all, of a module’s materials, one by one, so they can re-enter manufacturing supply chains as feedstock. Glass as clean glass cullet, aluminum as clean aluminum, silicon and silver as silicon and silver. Solar panels are inherently built to be encapsulated and durable enough to withstand the elements, which is exactly why the investment and technology required to recover each commodity cleanly, versus shredding an entire panel into smaller, layered, still [...] As one of the nation’s first solar recyclers handling volume at scale, and the first SEIA National Recycling Partners to be audited onsite by the association, we work to advance a stringent recycling standard created because we have seen what happens without it.

|
|  |
| 2. SPR employees oversee the solar panel recycling process, where end-of-life panels are processed to recover valuable materials and minimize waste. Source: |

## The Reuse Reality [...] ## Not All Solar Recycling Is Created Equal

Recycling in the solar industry has a problem worth discussing. Too often, low-technology or no-technology recyclers, only recover the high-value aluminum frame, all under the guise of recycling, while the other 90% of the panel is wasted, stockpiled, or exported. That is incomplete recycling, and it is more common than most asset owners realize.

items.title: New Jersey solar panel recycling system faces scrutiny after officials reveal limitation
items.summary:
Gard identified Commercial Solar Panel Recycling, based in Phillipsburg, as New Jersey's only authorized site that actually recycles panels, Resource Recycling reported. Four other locations send the panels they collect to the Phillipsburg facility, while the sixth uses an out-of-state facility it owns. [...] According to Resource Recycling, under the S3399 law, whoever owns, produces, distributes, or manufactures a piece of solar equipment is responsible for taking it back and recycling or refurbishing it once it reaches the end of its life. Then-Gov. Phil Murphy signed the measure on January 12. [...] ### Where can I learn more?

New Jersey's limited recycling options are part of a larger challenge: figuring out what to do with aging solar panels.

• Nearly 5 million retiring U.S. solar panels could become a strategic materials supply.

• U.S. solar recyclers recover valuable aluminum and silver, but low-silver panels threaten their business.

• Just 0.5% of a solar cell accounts for 47% of its recycling value.

turns.assistant_text:
The article titled **"Sungrow supports clean energy goals of a Northern Rivers solar panel recycling business"** discusses a partnership between Sungrow and ReSolve Global, a solar panel recycling business located in Northern Rivers, New South Wales. Sungrow has provided a 20 kWh battery and a 10 kW inverter to help ReSolve Global operate on clean, self-generated energy.

Key points from the article include:

- ReSolve Global aims to collect, assess, and sort used solar panels to prevent them from ending up in landfills and to recover valuable materials for reuse and recycling.
- The facility is designed to prioritize reuse wherever possible and responsibly recover remaining materials.
- By October 2026, ReSolve Global had already collected over 1,000 solar panels and is collaborating with local industries to develop pathways for reuse and recycling.
- Sungrow's support is seen as a step towards a circular solar industry, encouraging other businesses to adopt similar practices.

For more details, you can read the full article [here](https://www.pv-magazine-australia.com/2026/11/06/sungrow-supports-clean-energy-goals-of-a-new-northern-rivers-solar-panel-recycling-business).

# Sungrow supports clean energy goals of a Northern Rivers solar panel recycling business

Sungrow has partnered with Byron Bay solar panel recycling business ReSolve Global to ensure the new facility can run on clean, self-generated energy.

[![Ev Foley](https://www.pv-magazine-australia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Ev-Foley-e1789038228443.jpeg)](https://www.pv-magazine-australia.com/people-companies/ev-foley/)

By

[Ev Foley](https://www.pv-magazine-australia.com/people-companies/ev-foley/)

06 Nov 2026

- [Markets & Policy](https://www.pv-magazine-australia.com/category/markets-policy/)
- [Technology & Products](https://www.pv-magazine-australia.com/category/technology-products/)
- [Modules](https://www.pv-magazine-australia.com/tag/modules/)

![](https://www.pv-magazine-australia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/dismantling-line-1024x765.png)Image: ReSolve Global

China-headquartered solar inverter and energy storage system provider [Sungrow](https://www.pv-magazine-australia.com/2026/03/27/sungrow-unveils-integrated-solar-storage-solution-for-australian-market/) has partnered with new Northern Rivers region, New South Wales (NSW) solar [panel recycling](https://www.pv-magazine-australia.com/2026/10/30/panel-recycling-laws-needed-now-as-2035-million-tonne-solar-waste-mountain-looms/) business ReSolve Global to sponsor a 20 kWh SBH battery and 10 kW SH10RS inverter at the facility.

The SBH system pairs a hybrid energy storage solution with intelligent energy management, allowing ReSolve Global to store surplus solar generation and use it as needed for its operations while lowering costs and emissions.

![](https://www.pv-magazine-australia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/6c03d358-299e-4b96-a7c9-fb43d68d539f-1024x576.png)Sungrow’s solar plus storage system powering Resolve Global \| _Image: Sungrow_

Sungrow C&I Business Development Manager Richard Chen said solar has transformed how Australian homes and businesses generate power, and it’s the industry’s responsibility to make sure that equipment is managed well at the end of its life.

“ReSolve is doing exactly that, and we’re proud to support them. By powering their Tyagarah facility with a Sungrow SBH system and inverter, we’re helping ReSolve practise what it preaches: a recycling operation running on clean energy. It’s a meaningful step towards a truly circular solar industry, and we hope it inspires other businesses to follow,” Chen said.

Located 13 kilometres north of Byron Bay, and approximately 155 kilometres south of Brisbane, Queensland, ReSolve Global is housed in a 2,000-square-metre holding and sorting facility where used solar panels are collected, recorded, assessed and sorted, keeping used solar panels and other renewable-energy equipment out of landfill while recovering valuable materials for reuse and recycling.

ReSolve Global Director Ben Pietzch said it is the company’s goal to build a transparent and practical system that prioritises reuse wherever appropriate and ensures the remaining materials are responsibly recovered.

“Solar has delivered enormous benefits for Australian homes and businesses, but we also need to take responsibility for the equipment coming off rooftops,” Pietzsch said.

By the start of October 2026 when ReSolve Global began operations, it had already collected more than 1,000 solar panels and is working with local industry to develop pathways for panels to be reused where appropriate or responsibly recycled and their materials recovered.

It’s longer-term vision is to expand its resource-recovery model beyond solar panels to other renewable-energy inf
